_meta.description: Canonical geographic coverage dataset for Serbia (excluding Kosovo and Metohija). Every geographic crawl in this project iterates over this file.

sources.name: Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia — 2022 Census of Population, Households and Dwellings, data by municipalities and cities (G20234001)
sources.used_for: population (2022 census), area, settlement count, administrative district

sources.name: Wikipedia (sr) — Градови и општине Србије
sources.used_for: machine-readable transcription of the RZS 2022 census table

sources.name: Wikipedia (en) — Municipalities and cities of Serbia
sources.used_for: independent cross-check of the unit list against the Law on Territorial Organisation of the Republic of Serbia (Sl. glasnik RS 129/2007, 18/2016, 47/2018): 117 municipalities + 28 cities de facto

sources.name: RATEL numbering plan, via Wikipedia (en) — Telephone numbers in Serbia
Pošta Srbije postal code list, via Wikipedia (sr) — Списак поштанских бројева у Србији

_meta.authority_note: The unit list is cross-checked name by name at build time against the English Wikipedia list of municipalities and cities of Serbia, which is sourced from the Law on Territorial Organisation of the Republic of Serbia. The build fails if the two disagree. Both lists agree on all 145 local self-government units.
_meta.kosovo_note: The 28 municipalities of Kosovo and Metohija are deliberately excluded: they are not administered by Serbian institutions and are out of scope for this project.
_meta.priority_tier_rule: Computed over the 145 local self-government units by 2022 census population: tier 1 = the 20 most populous, tier 2 = population >= 20,000, tier 3 = the rest. Belgrade city municipalities are tiered separately — the 10 urban-core ones are tier 1, the 7 suburban ones are tier 2.
_meta.population_note: population is the 2022 census figure for the whole local self-government unit, not just its seat settlement. The Belgrade city municipalities marked population_census_year 2011 had no 2022 figure in the sources above.
_meta.postal_codes_note: postal_codes lists the code(s) of the municipal seat post office, not every code inside the unit.
_meta.landline_prefix_note: Serbian landline area codes are shared across a whole RATEL network group, so one prefix maps to many municipalities. landline_group_center marks the municipality a code is named after — use it when a landline number is the only location signal.
_meta.search_variants_note: Nominative, locative and genitive of the place name, each in both the diacritic and the ASCII-folded spelling. Serbian is inflected — listings say "fasader u Novom Sadu", not "fasader Novi Sad" — so a geographic query must be built from these variants, not from name_sr alone.
